knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Solid grid lines are one unit apart; dotted lines divide each square in half.

![](assets/6fe45e067793396c292e74cc88e434dc0ec249a452b9bf41fce3ebe70c1b9c73.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\lambda\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{3}{2}\,(-2, -1)=(-3, -\frac{3}{2}). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(-\frac{5}{2}, -5).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](assets/be1cdbb71d7dbe239733d3b35d5cf7b741394d6f3549e0dfd3affe61f8d7a8af.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{b}$, whose grid displacement is $(-2, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{-\frac{5}{2}}{-2}=\frac{5}{4} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-5}{-4}=\frac{5}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\frac{5}{4}\mathbf{b}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{5}{4}\mathbf{b} \\
&=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{5}{4}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{5}{4}$.

conversions: Reduce grid displacement ratio to a positive rational scalar

question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{1}{2}\,(2, 3)=(1, \frac{3}{2}). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(1, 1).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](assets/3034fb193a55d20f1442eacb43231f2f331e50dcd8339c28aa1011d22dcab5f8.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, 2)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}+\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a} \\
&=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{1}{2}$.
